title: The evaluation map of a module into its double dual is injective
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an arbitrary module M over a ring the evaluation map into the double dual with respect to the Pontryagin dual by Q/Z is injective (statement lines 13803-13806). The proof is a 9-line argument (proof lines 13809-13817) which uses that Q/Z is an injective abelian group: for a nonzero x in M one takes the cyclic subgroup it generates, produces a nonzero homomorphism from that subgroup to Q/Z that does not annihilate x, extends it to all of M by injectivity, and reads off that the evaluation of x at that extended homomorphism is nonzero. The two steps that carry the content are the existence of a nonzero map on the cyclic subgroup, which is a statement about Q/Z being divisible with enough elements, and its extension along the inclusion, which is the injectivity of Q/Z in the category of abelian groups. Both are standard and neither is proved here, but the argument is complete and short.
